title: Missed Call Text Back: The Cheapest Fix in Contractor Marketing
meta: An auto-text on every missed call is the cheapest lead recovery a contractor can buy. What to send, how fast, what it costs, and why it beats adding ad budget to a phone nobody answers.
short: The average shop misses 14% of its calls, and a homeowner with a leak does not leave a voicemail — they dial the next number. An automatic text sent the second you miss the call puts you back in the conversation before your competitor picks up. It costs a few dollars a month and recovers jobs you already paid to generate.
statLabel: Share of calls the average shop misses (CallRail 2026) — every one already cost you money

body.h2: You already paid for the call you just missed
body.answer: A missed call is a lead you bought and threw away.
body.html: Every ringing phone cost something to create — an ad, a review, a profile, a referral you earned. A booked job runs ~$542 through Angi versus ~$168 through Google Local Service Ads, and the average shop still misses 14% of its calls (CallRail 2026). That's not a phone problem, it's a budget problem: you're paying full price for leads and dropping one in seven on the floor. More on the size of it: what missed calls actually cost.

body.answer: They hang up and dial the next contractor.
body.html: Someone standing in two inches of water is not composing a message. 78% of homeowners hire whoever responds first (Lead Connect 2026), which means the winner of that job is usually decided in the next four minutes, without you. Voicemail is a system designed for a customer who no longer exists.

body.h2: What missed call text back actually is
body.answer: An automatic text fires the instant a call goes unanswered.
body.html: It's a setting, not a project. When a call rings out, your phone system sends the caller a text immediately — before they've finished dialing the next shop. Most VoIP providers, answering services, and contractor CRMs include it; standalone versions run a few dollars a month. If you do one thing to your marketing this month, do this one.

body.answer: Name the shop, apologize once, ask one question.
body.html: Three lines, no marketing voice: "This is Mike at Smith Heating & Air — sorry we missed you, we're on a job. What's going on and what's your address? I'll get you on the schedule." Naming the business stops it reading as spam, the apology buys ten seconds of patience, and one question gets them typing instead of dialing. Don't send a link. Don't send a form. Ask a question a person answers with their thumbs.

body.answer: Instant beats good; five minutes beats thirty.
body.html: The text has to fire in seconds, not after a five-minute delay someone helpfully configured. Replying in 5 minutes rather than 30 makes you up to 100x more likely to connect (MIT Sloan 2026), and an automatic text is the only way to hit that number while you're under a house. Then answer the reply like it's on fire — see why five minutes matters.

body.h2: Fix the phone before you raise the budget
body.answer: Ad spend on a broken phone is just faster waste.
body.html: Doubling your ad budget while missing 14% of calls buys you more missed calls. The order of operations never changes: answer the phone, then earn reviews, then fix the website, then spend. 98% of contractor-website visitors leave without calling (WebFX 2026) — the few who do call are the entire return on everything else you're paying for. Run your own number: the missed call revenue calculator.

faq.q: What is missed call text back?
faq.a: An automatic text message sent to a caller the moment their call goes unanswered, usually built into your VoIP system or contractor CRM. It puts you back in the conversation within seconds, which matters because 78% of homeowners hire whoever responds first (Lead Connect 2026).

faq.q: Do missed call text backs actually work for contractors?
faq.a: They recover leads you already paid to generate. The average shop misses 14% of its calls (CallRail 2026), homeowners with an urgent problem rarely leave voicemails, and replying in 5 minutes instead of 30 makes you up to 100x more likely to connect (MIT Sloan 2026).

faq.q: What should a missed call auto-text say?
faq.a: Name your business, apologize in one line, and ask one question: what's going on and what's the address. Keep it under three lines, skip links and forms, and make sure it fires in seconds rather than minutes.
